messages:
samir: FYI I just noticed an ingest-service JWT printed in a staging worker log during a debug run. snippet below.

samir: `... ingest_jwt=eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9...`

oncall-bot: Alert triggered by log-scan (rule: secret-like-token-in-logs). severity: medium. link: https://logs.internal/redwood/abcd1234

julia: where exactly was this? path?

samir: staging/worker-2026-03-19.log line ~942. I pulled the file and grepped for ingest_jwt. looks like a debug print left in by a recent deploy.

maria: ok first containment: rotate the staging ingest JWT and invalidate the current token. julia can you run rotation?

julia: on it. running: `redwoodctl secrets rotate --service ingest-service --env staging --force`

julia: rotated and invalidated. new token issued, old token revoked in auth service. response: 200.

kyle: good. can you also revoke any sessions that used that token? I want token usage logs scanned for the last 24h.

julia: running query on auth-logs: `SELECT * FROM auth_events WHERE token_kind='ingest_jwt' AND timestamp > now()-interval '24 hours'`

julia: result: only staging pod IPs, no external egress addresses. no customer API keys referenced.

samir: I also searched Sentry and artifact archives: found the same token in a compressed log bundle uploaded to staging-artifacts-bucket on 2026-03-19.

maria: schedule: delete the archive from S3, ensure lifecycle won't keep it. who has S3 access to that bucket?

julia: removed the archive copy, rotated bucket credentials used by the pipeline. filed internal ticket to sweep older bundles.

support-bot: Customer impact check: runbook asks to confirm if any production tokens were exposed.

kyle: confirmed this is staging-only. no production tokens exposed. mark impact: none. still file an incident and notify compliance.

samir: action items I propose: mask logger to prevent printing tokens, add lint rule to catch common secret var names, enable audit logging for secret rotations via KMS, and reduce default token scope for ingest-service.

maria: +1. also add RBAC change: only platform-admins and CI-bot can access ingest-service secrets; remove developer wide read.

julia: opened SEC-4321: "staging ingest JWT printed in logs" assign kyle, priority P2. includes: timeline, revocation, artifact purge, vuln triage and remediation tasks.

kyle: I'll own post-incident: update runbook with KMS envelope-wrapping example and add an automated CI check that fails when `ingest_jwt` or `ingest_token` appear in diffs.

samir: quick tech note for runbook: example mask config for our logger: `logger.addFilter(lambda r: re.sub(r'(?i)ingest(_)?jwt=[^\s]+','ingest_jwt=***', r.msg))`

maria: schedule a brief 30m review tomorrow 09:30 PT to triage follow-ups and confirm RBAC + KMS changes.

julia: added postmortem checklist to SEC-4321. next steps: close when runbook updated, lint in CI merged, and S3 artifact sweep completed.

kyle: thanks team. no customer comms needed per impact assessment but we'll keep audit trail and notify compliance. :white_check_mark:

samir: noted, will also add a small telemetry alert to detect tokens in logs that includes the source pod and commit id.

oncall-bot: Incident SEC-4321 created and linked to this thread.

maria: closing loop for now. if anyone finds any other re-uploads or similar prints, ping #incidents immediately.

julia: thanks, will follow up with PR numbers for the logger mask and CI lint.

kyle: moving to postmortem doc once the actionable items are done. good catch, samir. :eyes:
